paragraphs.text: translated by
1. MIGHTY are ye, and far-extended, Heaven and Earth: both Worlds are evermore to us like two young Dames.
paragraphs.original: महि द्यावापृथिवी भूतमुर्वी नारी यह्वी न रोदसी सदं नः ।
paragraphs.translit: mahi dyāvāpṛthivī bhūtamurvī nārī yahvī na rodasī sadaṃ naḥ |

paragraphs.text: Guard us thereby from stronger foe; guard us hereby to give us strength.
paragraphs.original: तेभिर्नः पातं सह्यस एभिर्नः पातं शूषणि
paragraphs.translit: tebhirnaḥ pātaṃ sahyasa ebhirnaḥ pātaṃ śūṣaṇi

paragraphs.text: 2. In each succeeding sacrifice that mortal honoureth the Gods,
paragraphs.original: यज्ञेयज्ञे स मर्त्यो देवान्सपर्यति ।
paragraphs.translit: yajñeyajñe sa martyo devānsaparyati |

paragraphs.text: He who, most widely known and famed for happiness, inviteth them.
paragraphs.original: यः सुम्नैर्दीर्घश्रुत्तम आविवासत्येनान्
paragraphs.translit: yaḥ sumnairdīrghaśruttama āvivāsatyenān

paragraphs.text: 3. Ye who are Rulers over all, great is your sovran power as Gods.
paragraphs.original: विश्वेषामिरज्यवो देवानां वार्महः ।
paragraphs.translit: viśveṣāmirajyavo devānāṃ vārmahaḥ |

paragraphs.text: Ye all possess all majesty: all must be served in sacrifice.
paragraphs.original: विश्वे हि विश्वमहसो विश्वे यज्ञेषु यज्ञियाः
paragraphs.translit: viśve hi viśvamahaso viśve yajñeṣu yajñiyāḥ

paragraphs.text: 4. These are the joyous Kings of Immortality, Parijman, Mitra, Aryaman, and Varuna.
paragraphs.original: ते घा राजानो अमृतस्य मन्द्रा अर्यमा मित्रो वरुणः परिज्मा ।
paragraphs.translit: te ghā rājāno amṛtasya mandrā aryamā mitro varuṇaḥ parijmā |

paragraphs.text: What else is Rudra, praised of men? the Maruts, Bhaga, Pusana?
paragraphs.original: कद्रुद्रो नृणां स्तुतो मरुतः पूषणो भगः
paragraphs.translit: kadrudro nṛṇāṃ stuto marutaḥ pūṣaṇo bhagaḥ

paragraphs.text: 5. Come also to our dwelling, Lords of ample wealth, common partakers of our waters, Sun and Moon,
paragraphs.original: उत नो नक्तमपां वृषण्वसू सूर्यामासा सदनाय सधन्या ।
paragraphs.translit: uta no naktamapāṃ vṛṣaṇvasū sūryāmāsā sadanāya sadhanyā |

paragraphs.text: When the great Dragon of the Deep hath settled down upon their floors.
paragraphs.original: सचा यत्साद्येषामहिर्बुध्नेषु बुध्न्यः
paragraphs.translit: sacā yatsādyeṣāmahirbudhneṣu budhnyaḥ

paragraphs.text: 6. And let the Asvins, Lords of splendour, set us free,- both Gods, and, with their Laws, Mitra and Varuna.
paragraphs.original: उत नो देवावश्विना शुभस्पती धामभिर्मित्रावरुणा उरुष्यताम् ।
paragraphs.translit: uta no devāvaśvinā śubhaspatī dhāmabhirmitrāvaruṇā uruṣyatām |

paragraphs.text: Through woes, as over desert lands, he speeds to ample opulence.
paragraphs.original: महः स राय एषतेऽति धन्वेव दुरिता
paragraphs.translit: mahaḥ sa rāya eṣate'ti dhanveva duritā

paragraphs.text: 7. Yea, let the Asvins Twain he gracious unto us, even Rudras, and all Gods, Bhaga, Rathaspati;
paragraphs.original: उत नो रुद्रा चिन्मृळतामश्विना विश्वे देवासो रथस्पतिर्भगः ।
paragraphs.translit: uta no rudrā cinmṛḷatāmaśvinā viśve devāso rathaspatirbhagaḥ |

paragraphs.text: Parijman, Rbhu, Vaja, O Lords of all wealth Rbhuksanas.
paragraphs.original: ऋभुर्वाज ऋभुक्षणः परिज्मा विश्ववेदसः
paragraphs.translit: ṛbhurvāja ṛbhukṣaṇaḥ parijmā viśvavedasaḥ

paragraphs.text: 8. Prompt is Rbhuksan, prompt the worshipper's strong drink: may thy fleet Bay Steeds, thine who speedest on, approach.
paragraphs.original: ऋभुरृभुक्षा ऋभुर्विधतो मद आ ते हरी जूजुवानस्य वाजिना ।
paragraphs.translit: ṛbhurṛbhukṣā ṛbhurvidhato mada ā te harī jūjuvānasya vājinā |

paragraphs.text: Not mans but God's is sacrifice whose psalm is unassailable.
paragraphs.original: दुष्टरं यस्य साम चिदृधग्यज्ञो न मानुषः
paragraphs.translit: duṣṭaraṃ yasya sāma cidṛdhagyajño na mānuṣaḥ

paragraphs.text: 9. O God Savitar, harmed by none, lauded, give us a place among wealthy princes.
paragraphs.original: कृधी नो अह्रयो देव सवितः स च स्तुषे मघोनाम् ।
paragraphs.translit: kṛdhī no ahrayo deva savitaḥ sa ca stuṣe maghonām |

paragraphs.text: With his Car-steeds at once 'hath our Indra guided the reins and the car of these men.
paragraphs.original: सहो न इन्द्रो वह्निभिर्न्येषां चर्षणीनां चक्रं रश्मिं न योयुवे
paragraphs.translit: saho na indro vahnibhirnyeṣāṃ carṣaṇīnāṃ cakraṃ raśmiṃ na yoyuve

paragraphs.text: 10. To these men present here, O Heaven and Earth, to us grant lofty fame extending over all mankind.
paragraphs.original: ऐषु द्यावापृथिवी धातं महदस्मे वीरेषु विश्वचर्षणि श्रवः ।
paragraphs.translit: aiṣu dyāvāpṛthivī dhātaṃ mahadasme vīreṣu viśvacarṣaṇi śravaḥ |

paragraphs.text: Give us a steed to win us strength, a steed with wealth for victory.
paragraphs.original: पृक्षं वाजस्य सातये पृक्षं रायोत तुर्वणे
paragraphs.translit: pṛkṣaṃ vājasya sātaye pṛkṣaṃ rāyota turvaṇe

paragraphs.text: 11. This speaker, Indra-for thou art our Friend-wherever he may be, guard thou, Victor! for help, ever for help
paragraphs.original: एतं शंसमिन्द्रास्मयुष्ट्वं कूचित्सन्तं सहसावन्नभिष्टये ।
paragraphs.translit: etaṃ śaṃsamindrāsmayuṣṭvaṃ kūcitsantaṃ sahasāvannabhiṣṭaye |

paragraphs.text: Thy wisdom, Vasu! prosper him.
paragraphs.original: सदा पाह्यभिष्टये मेदतां वेदता वसो
paragraphs.translit: sadā pāhyabhiṣṭaye medatāṃ vedatā vaso

paragraphs.text: 12. So have they strengthened this mine hymn which seems to take its bright path to the Sun, and reconciles the men:
paragraphs.original: एतं मे स्तोमं तना न सूर्ये द्युतद्यामानं वावृधन्त नृणाम् ।
paragraphs.translit: etaṃ me stomaṃ tanā na sūrye dyutadyāmānaṃ vāvṛdhanta nṛṇām |

paragraphs.text: Thus forms a carpenter the yoke of horses, not to be displaced.
paragraphs.original: संवननं नाश्व्यं तष्टेवानपच्युतम्
paragraphs.translit: saṃvananaṃ nāśvyaṃ taṣṭevānapacyutam

paragraphs.text: 13. Whose chariot-seat hath come again laden with wealth and bright with gold,
paragraphs.original: वावर्त येषां राया युक्तैषां हिरण्ययी ।
paragraphs.translit: vāvarta yeṣāṃ rāyā yuktaiṣāṃ hiraṇyayī |

paragraphs.text: Lightly, with piercing ends, as 'twere two ranks of heroes ranged for fight.
paragraphs.original: नेमधिता न पौंस्या वृथेव विष्टान्ता
paragraphs.translit: nemadhitā na pauṃsyā vṛtheva viṣṭāntā

paragraphs.text: 14. This to Duhsima Prthavana have I sung, to Vena, Rama, to the nobles, and the King.
paragraphs.original: प्र तद्दुःशीमे पृथवाने वेने प्र रामे वोचमसुरे मघवत्सु ।
paragraphs.translit: pra tadduḥśīme pṛthavāne vene pra rāme vocamasure maghavatsu |

paragraphs.text: They yoked five hundred, and their love of us was famed upon their way.
paragraphs.original: ये युक्त्वाय पञ्च शतास्मयु पथा विश्राव्येषाम्
paragraphs.translit: ye yuktvāya pañca śatāsmayu pathā viśrāvyeṣām

paragraphs.text: 15. Besides, they showed us seven -and-seventy horses here.
paragraphs.original: अधीन्न्वत्र सप्ततिं च सप्त च ।
paragraphs.translit: adhīnnvatra saptatiṃ ca sapta ca |

paragraphs.text: Tanva at once displayed his gift, Parthya at once displayed his gift; and straightway Mayava showed his.
paragraphs.original: सद्यो दिदिष्ट तान्वः सद्यो दिदिष्ट पार्थ्यः सद्यो दिदिष्ट मायवः
paragraphs.translit: sadyo didiṣṭa tānvaḥ sadyo didiṣṭa pārthyaḥ sadyo didiṣṭa māyavaḥ
